The Endangered Species Act (ESA) establishes a legal framework for conserving species and ecosystems that are at risk of extinction. Its primary legal implication is the imposition of a duty on federal agencies. Specifically, any federal agency must ensure that any action they authorize, fund, or carry out does not jeopardize the continued existence of any species listed as endangered or threatened, nor does it destroy or adversely modify the designated critical habitat for those species. This requirement serves as a protective barrier, mandating that federal projects undergo scrutiny to prevent harm to protected wildlife and their essential environments.

Regarding your question about the day that comes after Monday: Tuesday.
